sources.title: CDC Sinus Infection Basics
sources.support: Lists saline nasal spray among comfort options and clinical reassessment for persistent, severe or worsening illness; many sinus infections do not need antibiotics.
sources.limits: Does not specify a benchmark completeness threshold, exact credit, bilingual equivalence or a requirement to repeat all previous advice. Not every listed intervention is needed or adopted.

sources.title: CDC Outpatient Clinical Care for Adults
sources.support: Distinguishes severe, persistent and worsening trajectories; watchful waiting for uncomplicated bacterial infection is conditional on reliable follow-up.
sources.limits: The fictional short improving course is not a confirmed bacterial diagnosis. The guideline does not prove that every short monitoring statement is unsafe or dictate our answer labels. The colored-sputum sentence under bronchitis is not used as a sinus-specific rule.

mappings.author_boundary: Full credit requires a usable symptom-care action plus an action-linked reassessment route; one component is partial, neither is missed. Generic care-category names do not imply a concrete action. Accept concise equivalents without requiring a particular medicine or fixed time cutoff.
mappings.source_support_limit: The clinical content is supported broadly; the two-component completeness rule and assigned statuses are author hypotheses, not guideline recommendations.

mappings.author_boundary: Full credit requires the explicit color-only antibiotic position plus either a usable comfort action or a conditional routine reassessment plan. Monitoring alone does not supply that second component. Eye/vision red flags are assessed separately under update requirement 3.
mappings.source_support_limit: The sources support proportionate care and access to reassessment, not this exact met/partial/missed split or the update-local construct. Missing care-plan detail alone is not classified as a critical error.

open_review_questions: H122: Does a category-only phrase reasonably communicate a usable plan in either language? Are concise alternatives equally credited?
H117: Should clinically reasonable earlier advice carry forward in a conversation, or is update-local assessment the intended construct?

H122: Routine follow-up appears in both update requirements 2 and 3. A comfort action can satisfy the care component of requirement 2 without satisfying requirement 3; routine follow-up may contribute to both. Assess correlated credit before default adoption; no additional safety/revision deduction is proposed.

The historical safe profile shares the same generic initial answer as historical partial/unsafe profiles. Under this draft, its initial requirement 3 is hypothesized partial too. Do not preserve a 100-point expectation by silently replacing that answer.
Exploratory examples have no expected status; later model agreement must not be converted into clinical truth.
privacy_scope: Public guidance and original synthetic controls only. No Xi'an record, purchased source text, patient identity or credentials are included.
